text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
- After Chancellor Helmut Kohl's top deputy Wolfgang Schaueble offers new talks over tax reform plans, the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) wait with new conditions.
- Chancellor Kohl wants to delay a decision over a possible cabinet reshuffle until the end of the year.
- Poland's ambassador to Bonn, Andrzej Byrt, thanks Germans for their help for flood victims.
- Wage costs as a percentage of firms' turnover have sunk steadily since 1993 according to the German Federation of Trade Unions (DGB).

- Bundesbank vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum says the central bank has changed its way of announcing its third key rate, saying it wants to forego the practice of early release of conditions for setting its weekly securities repurchase rate, or repo.
- Kohl will not rule out the possibility of a cabinet reshuffle.
- Labour Minister Norbert Bluem declares the new, lower minimum wage agreed in July for the building sector to be generally binding with effect from September.
- German diversified utility RWE AG surprises with plans to abolish multiple voting rights on shares mainly held by local municipalities.
- Ruling coalition presents revised tax reform plans for discussion with opposition SPD in second round of parliamentary mediation talks.
- Kohl won't rule out possibility of cabinet reshuffle.
- Saxony state wants to step up the fight against right-wing extremism.
